correctness.rationale: Diagonalizing the two-node Gram matrix gives a symmetric bounded component and antisymmetric denominator 1-exp(-λ|δ|^α). The mean difference m(u+δ/2)-m(u-δ/2)=m′(u)δ+o(δ), yielding weight blow-up proportional to |δ|^(1-α) when α>1. Gaussian noise therefore has one-sided regularly varying tails with exponent β=1/(α-1) and constant (σ/λ)^β Γ((β+1)/2)/√π ∫|m′|^β. Integrability gives finite second moment iff α<3/2, including logarithmic divergence at α=3/2. The nugget integral reduces to ∫ d²/(η+λd^α)² dd, giving the stated log coefficient or gamma-product power coefficient for α>3/2; bounded Lipschitz noiseless contribution cannot alter tail leading terms. Independently checked kernel-mean/weight collision scaling at α=1.25,1.75,2.0 via direct numerical integration; no numerical test is a uniform proof.
